title: Healthscore Playbook — KPI Recipes for Renewals and QBRs
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, annotated collection of KPI “recipes” for use in QBRs and renewal conversations. The goal is to go beyond definitions — give CS teams ready-to-drop-in calculation snippets, alert triggers, and remediation playbooks so metric conversations are consistent across accounts.

Audience:
Customer Success Managers, Renewal Owners, Solutions Engineers, GTM leaders preparing QBR slides and renewal health packs.

How to use the recipes:
- Pick the metric(s) relevant to the account (latency + cost for performance-heavy customers; cache hit + latency for aggressive cost optimization customers).
- Use the sample SQL/pseudocode to generate the charts for the last 90 / 30 / 7 day windows.
- Attach the remediation steps as suggested playbook items in the QBR slide with owners.

Metric Recipe 1 — Latency (generation time)
- Why it matters: Perceived responsiveness drives product adoption and affects SLOs; tail latency impacts interactive workflows.
- Definition: Server-side generation time per request. Primary signals: P50, P95, P99 over 7/30/90 day windows.
- Measurement window: rolling 7d for ops, 30d for trend.
- Sample calculation (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day,
         percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gen_ms) AS p50_ms,
         percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gen_ms) AS p95_ms,
         percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gen_ms) AS p99_ms
  FROM requests
  WHERE customer_id = '{{account}}' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY day
  ORDER BY day;
- Alerting heuristic: p95 > 1200ms sustained for 30m or increase > 40% vs baseline.
- Quick remediations: check model routing, fallback to a faster variant, validate batching params, increase dedicated capacity during peak windows.

Metric Recipe 2 — Uptime (service and model route availability)
- Why it matters: SLA and renewal conversations; measures reliability of production feature.
- Definition: Percentage of successful requests (2xx) per route / per model divided by total routed requests in window. Exclude scheduled maintenance windows.
- Measurement window: 30d rolling and last billing period.
- Sample calculation:
  uptime = 1 - (error_count / total_requests) * 100
- Alerting heuristic: uptime < 99.5% for 30d or a single-day drop below 98% triggers RCA.
- Owner: SRE/Platform -> escalated via PS if persistent.

Metric Recipe 3 — Cost per token (and effective customer TCO view)
- Why it matters: Cost transparency maps to renewal economics and upsell conversations.
- Definition: (infrastructure_amortized_cost + model_license_cost + orchestration_cost) / billed_tokens. For embeddings treat 1 embedding unit = 1 billed unit.
- Measurement window: monthly (billing cycle).
- Calculation hints: include explicit fields showing token type (prompt vs completion), estimated KV cache savings, and amortized GPU hours.
- Example breakdown lines to show execs:
  - Raw tokens: 12,435,000
  - Approx. GPU-hours: 42.3  -> (x $/gpu-hr) = $3,780
  - Cache savings (estimated): 18% fewer completion tokens = $680 saved
  - Net cost/token = (infra + license - savings) / billed_tokens = $0.00043/token
- Alerting heuristic: month-over-month cost per token increase > 25% without a corresponding quality improvement.

Metric Recipe 4 — Cache hit rate (prefix + KV)
- Why it matters: Cache is the most reliable lever to reduce unit cost while preserving latency.
- Definition: cache_hit_requests / cache_eligible_requests (report both request-level and token-level hit rates).
- Measurement window: 7d rolling for ops, 30d trend for business.
- Sample calculation:
  token_hit_rate = 1 - (missed_tokens / cache_eligible_tokens)
- Recommended targets: Growth customers: token-level hit >= 22%; Enterprise: >= 30% (depends on workload).
- Remediation: increase prefix caching TTL for stable prompts, introduce shared prompt templates, serve hybrid cache (shared + per-account).

KPI Template (copy into QBR slide or sheet) — CSV-ready rows:
metric,window,target,threshold-alert,owner,why,example-action
Latency P95,30d,<=800ms,>1200ms:email-sre,CS-rep,Model change / routing fallback
Uptime (route),30d,>=99.9%,<99.5%:escalate-sre,SRE,Open RCA + maintenance schedule
Cost per token,monthly,<=$0.0005,>0.00065:review-cost,CS-rep+Solutions,Quantize / caching / route to cheaper variant
Cache token-hit,7d,>=22%,<15%:cache-review,Solutions,Increase TTL / template re-use

Example account play (Growth customer) — what to present in QBR:
- Topline: 30d latency p95 = 720ms (target met), p99 = 1.8s (one spike on 2026-01-14)
- Reliability: route uptime = 99.87% (no major incidents), maintenance windows accounted for 0.03% downtime
- Cost: net cost/token = $0.00048 (down 9% MoM due to cache config)
- Opportunity: Increase prefix cache TTL for top-3 flows -> projected 12% token reduction -> estimated $8k/quarter savings
- Asks: approve 2-week canary to bump TTL + Solutions to run prompt-template audit (owner: Priya Desai)

Notes on data quality and caveats:
- Separate observability signals (ingress latency) from generation latency; present both when possible.
- Exclude synthetic/test traffic and retries from numerator.
- Cache "eligibility" must be computed consistently (define per-route rules).
- When showing cost, clearly call out assumptions (gpu $/hr, amortization window, license allocation).

Quick checklist for QBR prep (copyable):
- [ ] Run SQL snippets for 7/30/90d windows and attach graphs
- [ ] Add mini-RCA for any p95/p99 spikes in last 30d
- [ ] Pull billing cost breakdown and show token vs GPU split
- [ ] Recommend 1–3 concrete ops items (TTL change, route pin, quantization trial) with owners

Appendix — small repo of useful queries and PR links:
- Baseline latency query: (see recipe 1 sample)
- Cost breakdown helper (pseudo): SELECT sum(gpu_cost + infra_cost + license) AS total_cost, sum(billed_tokens) AS tokens FROM billing WHERE customer_id = '{{account}}' AND period = '{{month}}'
- Related tickets: CS-412 (renewal prep kit), CS-521 (cache telemetry gaps)

Revision notes:
- v0.1 2024-07-12 initial draft (A. Patel)
- v0.4 2025-03-02 added cost amortization guidance (Priya)
- v0.7 2025-11-18 added token-level cache targets (Marcus)
- v1.0 2026-02-20 cleanup and canonical templates for QBR decks

If you want, I can also generate a slide-ready CSV and a copyable SQL file for a particular account — tell me an account id and 30d window and I'll produce the graphs-ready exports.
